subject: Science
title: Sense games
objectives: Children will use different senses at stations to explore objects.
Children will link a sense to a body part.
content: Using different senses at stations, a mystery bag and linking each sense to a body part.
teachingActivities: Run stations with simple rules; ask which sense the child used; point to the body part each time; use the same five picture cards daily.
learnerActivities: Use different senses to explore objects and link each sense to a body part.
resources: Five sense picture cards: eye, ear, hand, nose, tongue
assessment: Observe whether each child names at least three senses and points to the right body part.
expectedOutcomes: Names at least three senses with support.
Points to the body part for each sense.

lessons.title: Five senses song
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will sing a song about the five senses and touch the matching body part.
successCriteria: Touches the body part for each sense
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have explored seeing, hearing, touch, smell and taste separately.
lessons.starter: Hold up the eye card and say "We see with our eyes." Touch your eyes.
teacherActivities: Show each card and touch the body part: eyes, ears, hands, nose, tongue.
Sing "I see with my eyes, I hear with my ears" and show each card.
Sing again and let children hold the cards.
Let a child lead with the doll.
learnerActivities: Children touch the same part.
Children listen and touch each part.
Child holds up the card at the right word.
Child touches the doll and friends copy.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each card and touch the body part: eyes, ears, hands, nose, tongue. Children: Children touch the same part.
Step 2. Teacher: Sing "I see with my eyes, I hear with my ears" and show each card. Children: Children listen and touch each part.
Step 3. Teacher: Sing again and let children hold the cards. Children: Child holds up the card at the right word.
Step 4. Teacher: Let a child lead with the doll. Children: Child touches the doll and friends copy.

practical.title: Five senses
steps: Sit in a circle with five cards.
Sing the song and touch each body part.
Hold up the card at the right word.
practical.safety: Keep actions gentle and fingers away from eyes. Leave space between children.

differentiation.support: Touch the part together and say the sense.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to lead and choose the sense.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Names senses and body parts with support
lessons.homeConnection: Sing the five senses song at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sing a song about the five senses and touch the matching body part" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: I see with my eyes, I hear with my ears, I touch with my hands.

lessons.title: Sense stations
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will use different senses at stations to explore objects.
successCriteria: Uses the right sense at each station
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have explored seeing, hearing, touch, smell and taste separately.
resources: Five stations: look, listen, touch, smell and a picture tasting station with a lemon picture
lessons.starter: Show the five stations and say "Today we use all our senses."
teacherActivities: Visit each station with the whole group and say which sense to use.
Let children explore at their own pace at each station.
Ask "Which sense did you use?" at each.
Come together and name one thing from each station.
learnerActivities: Children look, listen, touch and smell as shown.
Child explores and talks.
Child points to the body part.
Child names an object.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Visit each station with the whole group and say which sense to use. Children: Children look, listen, touch and smell as shown.
Step 2. Teacher: Let children explore at their own pace at each station. Children: Child explores and talks.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Which sense did you use?" at each. Children: Child points to the body part.
Step 4. Teacher: Come together and name one thing from each station. Children: Child names an object.

practical.title: Sense stations
steps: Name the sense and the body part.
practical.safety: Use only safe objects and supervise each station. Keep the tasting station as pictures only unless allergies have been checked.

differentiation.support: Stay with the child at each station and name the sense.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to teach a friend a station.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the objects away and say "Thank you, senses."
lessons.homeConnection: Use all your senses on a walk at home and talk about them.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use different senses at stations to explore objects" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: The big mystery bag
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will use touch and smell to guess what is in the bag.
successCriteria: Feels an object in a bag
Names the object or says a word about it
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have explored seeing, hearing, touch, smell and taste separately.
resources: A sponge, an orange, a spoon and a toy car
lessons.starter: Show the bag and say "There is something in my bag. Use your hand to feel it."
teacherActivities: Put the sponge in the bag. Show a child how to feel it without looking.
Ask "Is it soft or hard?" and "What do you think it is?"
Take it out and say "It is a sponge."
Repeat with the orange, spoon and toy car.
learnerActivities: Child feels the object.
Child says a word or guesses.
Children look and check.
Each child feels and guesses.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Put the sponge in the bag. Show a child how to feel it without looking. Children: Child feels the object.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Is it soft or hard?" and "What do you think it is?" Children: Child says a word or guesses.
Step 3. Teacher: Take it out and say "It is a sponge." Children: Children look and check.
Step 4. Teacher: Repeat with the orange, spoon and toy car. Children: Each child feels and guesses.

practical.title: Mystery bag
steps: Put one object in the bag.
practical.safety: Use clean, large objects only and make sure no object is sharp. Supervise the bag.

differentiation.support: Offer two choices and describe the object first.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to put a secret object in for a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the objects back and say thank you.
lessons.homeConnection: Play the mystery bag game at home with safe objects.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use touch and smell to guess what is in the bag" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Which sense?
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will match activities to the sense they use.
successCriteria: Names the sense for an action
Points to the matching body part
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have explored seeing, hearing, touch, smell and taste separately.
resources: Action pictures: looking, listening, touching, sniffing, eating
lessons.starter: Say "I am looking at a book. Which sense?" and point to your eyes.
teacherActivities: Show an action picture and say what the child is doing.
Ask "Which sense?" and wait for children to point to the card or body part.
Do an action yourself and ask which sense.
Let each child do an action for friends to match.
learnerActivities: Children look and listen.
Child points to the right card.
Children point to the matching body part.
Child acts and friends match.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show an action picture and say what the child is doing. Children: Children look and listen.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Which sense?" and wait for children to point to the card or body part. Children: Child points to the right card.
Step 3. Teacher: Do an action yourself and ask which sense. Children: Children point to the matching body part.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child do an action for friends to match. Children: Child acts and friends match.

practical.title: Match the sense
steps: Put five sense cards on the floor.
Children stand by the matching card.
practical.safety: Keep the floor clear and children seated between turns. Supervise movement.

differentiation.support: Offer two sense cards and say the sense first.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make up an action for a sense.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What sense do you use to listen?
What sense do you use to eat?

expectedOutcomes: Matches actions to senses with support
lessons.conclusion: Put the cards away and say "Five senses."
lessons.homeConnection: Ask your child which sense they use at home during the day.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "match activities to the sense they use" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 5 senses check
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child uses the senses and links them to body parts.
successCriteria: Points to the body part for each sense
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have explored seeing, hearing, touch, smell and taste separately.
lessons.starter: Sing the five senses song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: look and listen, touch and smell, sense cards.
At each station ask "Which sense?" and watch what the child does.
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child answers with a word or point.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: look and listen, touch and smell, sense cards. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "Which sense?" and watch what the child does. Children: Child answers with a word or point.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Senses stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use safe objects only.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use three senses.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to name all five senses.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: names senses; points to the matching body part; uses senses to describe objects.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 5
Names senses and body parts with support
lessons.conclusion: Sing the senses song once more and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about senses at home during daily routines.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child uses the senses and links them to body parts" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
